tagline.text: A figure-eight mountain lake in Siaton, born from a 1925 earthquake landslide

location.label: Location
location.text: Mountain area of Managobsob, Siaton, Negros Oriental

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person from Dumaguete, including transport, entrance, boats and meals)

children.text: Lake Balanan is a freshwater lake of about 25 hectares at roughly 237 m above sea level in the mountains of Siaton, southern Negros Oriental. It formed when an earthquake blocked a river in 1925, and today you can kayak, ride raft-style boats and walk toward waterfalls. It makes an easy half-day trip from Dumaguete.
Lake Balanan is a freshwater lake tucked into the mountains of the municipality of Siaton in southern Negros Island. It sits at about
above sea level and covers roughly 25 hectares. The lake is pinched in the middle into a figure-eight shape, and at its narrowest point it is only about

wide, so from above it looks like two lakes joined together. In a part of Negros where most trips revolve around beaches, a forest-and-lake landscape like this is a welcome change and fits nicely into a one-day plan. It is about 60 km south of Dumaguete, so travelers coming from Manila or Cebu can simply use Dumaguete as a base. Many visitors pair the seaside towns along the Siaton coast and the mountain lake on separate days.
This is not a natural lake but one made by a disaster. On

, a magnitude 6.8 earthquake shook Siaton and triggered a landslide that dammed the Balanan River, and water rose behind the blockage to form today's lake. Locals reportedly called this dam Sampong. Three streams, the Lamarao, Balanan and Nasig-id creeks, feed the northern end of the lake, and the water drains out through the Balanan River.

The surrounding forest is home to wildlife including bats, and the lake and forest are managed as a watershed area. In 1987, DENR Region 7 endorsed a proposal to declare the area a game refuge and wildlife sanctuary. In other words, think of it not as a theme park but as a modest retreat, with lodging and boating facilities set inside a conservation area.

Even so, it is wise to lower your expectations a little. A February 2024 column in a Dumaguete newspaper pointed out neglect, including a murky man-made swimming pool and a staircase to the waterfalls that had washed away. By contrast, a February 2025 traveler review described calm water and almost no crowds, a good place to relax quietly. The facilities are simple, but the peace and quiet is the real draw. For that reason this guide does not state prices and facilities as certain, and instead notes the source year alongside each one. Please check the latest situation before you go.

blocks.title: A figure-eight lake born of an earthquake

children.text: Because the lake was created by a 1925 landslide that blocked a river, its shape is distinctive. The narrowest neck is only about
wide, and walking along the shore keeps changing the view, so it never gets dull.
On the calm water you can rent kayaks, small paddle boats (bancas) and pedal boats by the hour. According to a 2018 guide, a kayak cost
per hour, so confirm current prices on site.
A forest path of about
4 km
is described as circling the lake. It is an easy walk, but it gets slippery after rain.

There are waterfalls on Lamarao Creek and Balanan Creek, and you can walk from the lake edge toward them. A 2024 report said the stairs to the falls had been washed away, so ask about the condition of the path first.
You can rent a floating cottage or raft on the lake by the hour and eat a packed lunch while relaxing. Picnic tables are usually available as an all-day rental.
According to a 2016 guide, there is a zipline across the lake. It is safest to confirm whether it is operating, and the price, before your visit.

blocks.title: A night in the forest and camping

children.text: The lakeside has guest rooms, a staff house, a treehouse and a campground. After dark the mobile signal is weak, which makes it a good place to focus on the stars and the sounds of the forest.
The surrounding forest is known to hold a large bat population. If you sit quietly at dusk, you can feel the mood of the forest change.

items.title: Day trip from Dumaguete
items.subtitle: A half-day to full-day trip by bus and motorcycle taxi

children.text: Take an air-conditioned bus toward Siaton from the Ceres bus terminal in Dumaguete. Tell the driver in advance to drop you at the highway junction before Siaton town.
From the junction, take a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) up about
10 km
of mountain road to the lake. The road is steep and rough, so agree on the fare with the driver first.
Pay the entrance fee at the gate, go down to the lakeshore and rent a kayak or banca for about an hour.
Walk the lakeside trail through the forest, and if the way is passable, make a short trip toward the waterfalls. Ask the staff about the condition of the path.
Have lunch at the lakeside restaurant. Reviews say food can take over an hour when the kitchen is busy, so order as soon as you arrive.
Take a habal-habal back down to the highway junction and catch a bus to Dumaguete. The last bus may leave early, so start back no later than 4 p.m.
Using only public transport, the round-trip travel alone takes about four hours. To save time, hire a vehicle for the day in Dumaguete.

items.title: Two days, one night
items.subtitle: A route that lets you sleep by the lake and see it in the morning

children.text: Leave Dumaguete by car or van and reach the lake after about an hour and a half.
After lunch, check in, drop your bags and spend the afternoon on kayaks and the floating cottage.
At dusk, stroll along the shore listening to the forest.
Next morning, kayak on the misty lake, have breakfast and check out.
Book your room and order meals by phone in advance. The signal is weak, so contacting anyone on site is difficult.
There are direct flights from Manila (MNL) to Sibulan Airport, Dumaguete (DGT). Check the airline's latest announcements for operating days and times.
From the airport, take a tricycle or taxi into Dumaguete city.
You can also reach Dumaguete port by ferry from Cebu or Manila.
From the Ceres bus terminal in Dumaguete, take a bus toward Siaton or Bayawan. The distance is about
60 km
and the trip takes about
2 hours
According to a 2018 guide, the air-conditioned bus fare was about
. It may have changed since.
Get off at the highway junction in Siaton where a sign points to the lake.

items.title: From the junction to the lake

children.text: From the junction to the lake it is about
10 km
of steep mountain road. Use a motorcycle taxi or tricycle.
Reviews from 2016 to 2018 put the fare at about
one way. Settle the price before you board.
From Dumaguete, follow the coastal road toward Siaton and turn onto the mountain road at the signpost. It takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
The mountain road is narrow and rough, so an SUV or van suits it better than a regular car.

The dry season from November to April is the most comfortable. The mountain road is less slippery and the lake water looks clearer. In the rainy season the road turns muddy, and after heavy rain the waterfalls swell and can be hard to reach.
Several guides say entrance is free on Tuesdays, but it has not been confirmed that this still applies. Weekday mornings are the quietest.

The sun sets early in the mountains, so the forest darkens quickly in the late afternoon. Going up around 9 a.m. and coming down around 3 p.m. balances travel and rest well. Weekends and holidays may bring more local family groups, so choose a weekday if you want quiet.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The best time for walking and kayaking.
Early morning or late afternoon is best.
Paths can be slippery and the waterfalls hard to reach.

items.label: Entrance fee
items.note: 2016 and 2018 guides and recent reviews are similar (no official rate sheet); about ₱25 for children, students and seniors

items.label: Kayak
items.note: 2018 guide ₱150 (2 people), around-2025 review ₱150~200. Confirm on site

items.label: Meals
items.note: Mains are big enough for 2-3 people to share

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
The lakeside has guest rooms, a staff house, a treehouse and a campground. According to a 2018 guide, a big room cost about
(4 people) and a small room about
(3 people). If you want comfortable lodging, it is better to stay in Dumaguete or Siaton town and make this a day trip.
Meals are served at the lakeside restaurant. According to reviews, breakfast ran about
and mains about
, with generous portions. When the kitchen is busy it can take over an hour, so order as soon as you arrive. It is a good idea to bring snacks and water.

Siaton town has small eateries and a market, so you can buy a simple lunch or snacks before you head up. There are few shops by the lake in the mountains, so bring plenty of water and snacks. Nights in the forest can feel cooler than the day, so pack a light jacket.

Before you visit, phone the Negros Oriental tourism office or the Siaton tourism office to confirm whether the site is operating and what the rates are. Phone numbers quoted in old reviews may be out of date.
Many reviews mention a weak mobile signal. Save your maps offline and bring a power bank.
Bring plenty of cash. Cards and e-payments may not be accepted.
Wear non-slip sandals or sneakers. The paths are steep and have wet stretches.
Bring insect repellent. It is a forest, and mosquitoes are common.
When you go up by motorcycle taxi, agree on a pickup time for the return or get the driver's contact number. It is hard to find a ride at the lake.
If you come with children, keep them beside you at all times. The terrain is steep and some lakeside spots have no railings.
If your group is large, hiring a van for the day in Dumaguete is more comfortable and saves time compared with changing between a bus and motorcycles.
Things may get wet, so bring a change of clothes and a waterproof bag, and keep your camera and phone in a waterproof pouch when kayaking.
Swimming in the lake is reported to be prohibited, so use only the designated pools.
A 2018 guide said the lake holds electric eels and that only staff may swim in it. Check the current rule on site.
A 2024 report said the artificial pool's water quality was poor and the stairs to the falls had washed away. The condition of facilities is not consistent.
The mountain road is narrow, steep and rough, and dangerous in the rainy season. Postpone your trip if it rains.
The last public transport leaves early. We recommend heading down before 4 p.m.
Always wear a life jacket and never stand up in a boat.
A seaside town south of Dumaguete known for its beaches and diving. It takes at least about
1 hour 30 minutes
by vehicle.
An island famous for sea turtles and snorkeling. You reach it by boat from a port near Dumaguete.
The transport hub with the airport and bus terminal, and the starting point for the road to Siaton.
A quiet beach town in southwestern Negros. You can consider it as a follow-on stop after Siaton.
